title: Control: one person standing still, off to the side - a ~25th-percentile person (COCO 124442)
purpose: Typical-person variant of s15_static_offset. The published person cells were built with COCO 19432/428692, which the 2026-09-15 person fidelity study places at the 98.5-100th percentile of rendered detectability among 266 real people. This scene is that scene with a ~25th-percentile person in it and nothing else changed, so a flight against it measures how much of the published 0.97-0.99 tracking fraction is a property of the subject rather than of the perception system. Not part of the acceptance matrix; run_acceptance2.sh does not reference it.

subjects.name: subj_person_target
subjects.note: TYPICAL-PERSON VARIANT, 2026-09-15. Byte-identical to s15_static_offset.json except for the COCO cutout: img 124442/ann 1238296 replaces img 19432/ann 428692. Same subject name, same role, same height_m 1.7, same pos, same motion, same lighting, same expected_behaviour (target and gates), same matte floor. The panel's WIDTH follows from the cutout's own bbox aspect (2.388 h/w -> 0.7119 m at 1.7 m tall, against the flown cutout's 2.627 -> 0.647 m); that is a property of which person it is, not an independent change, and it is the only geometric consequence. WHY THIS PERSON: a ~25th-percentile person. Rendered through build_scene's own cutout pipeline at s15's geometry it sits at the 28.4th percentile of the 266-person cohort of docs/eval_results/2026-09-15-sim-person-fidelity (per range 71.4/52.3/19.9/20.7/0.0/6.0), against the flown cutout's 99.2nd. Its own photograph scores 0.5895 on the chip arm through the resolution-matched chain, the 10.4th percentile of 48 size-matched whole-upright photographs. Selection is docs/eval_results/2026-09-15-typical-person/scripts/pick_subjects.py; no score was re-computed for it.

prediction.rationale: The fidelity study's static-frame result predicts more time below the 0.45 exit bar than the flown cutout ever shows (0 of 282 frames), but it states explicitly that per-frame rates cannot be multiplied into a loss-of-track fraction, because consecutive frames are correlated and the follower has hysteresis. That is what this flight measures.
